title: Lesson 13: Handover That Makes the Client Self-Sufficient: Operating Docs and Runbooks
description: Handing over ownership rather than just files: an operating doc that captures how the system is configured, runbooks a calm stranger can execute under pressure, finished with a dry run and a support taper.

questions.question: How do the operating doc and the runbook differ?
options: The operating doc is the recovery procedure for failures, and the runbook is the reference for how it is configured
The operating doc is calm reference for configuration, and the runbook is procedure for when it breaks
The operating doc is written for the client, and the runbook is written only for the original builder
The operating doc is written under pressure, and the runbook is written calmly beforehand
questions.explanation: The operating doc answers how the system is put together and configured, read calmly. The runbook answers what to do when something broke, written calmly but read in a hurry by a stranger.

questions.question: How is a handover proven to be real?
options: When the client signs a form confirming that each of the delivered files has been received
When the consultant narrates the demo and the client agrees that the system works
When an unbriefed operator recovers a failed run from the docs while you stay silent
When the documentation has been reviewed and formally approved by the consultant
questions.explanation: Files are not ownership; the ability to run, change, and recover is. The handover passes when a stranger executes the recovery procedure to a successful end without a prompt from you.

questions.question: How should credentials appear in the operating doc?
options: As their actual values, so that the operator can confirm each one directly
As their existence, location, and owner, never their value
Omitted entirely from the doc, so that nothing sensitive is ever written down
As an encrypted block that the operator decrypts whenever it is needed
questions.explanation: The doc records what exists and where it lives so the operator knows what to refresh and whom to ask. Writing the value in turns a configuration note into a breach.
